title: Dzungar Khanate
capsule: The Dzungar Khanate was the last great nomadic empire of Central Asia, formed when the Oirat Choros tribal leader Khara Khula consolidated the western Mongol (Oirat) confederacy in the early 17th century; it expanded dramatically under Galdan Khan (r. 1676–1697), who seized control of the Tarim Basin and attacked Qing-allied Khalkha Mongols, drawing Kangxi Emperor into three major campaigns (1690, 1696, 1697) that culminated in Galdan's defeat at Zuunmod in 1696. At its height c. 1700–1745 the khanate controlled territory from the Altai Mountains to the Pamirs, including Xinjiang and the Ili Valley. The Qianlong Emperor launched a final extermination campaign in 1755–1757; the Dzungar people were largely destroyed by Qing forces and epidemic disease, and by 1758 Dzungar political existence had ended completely.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Dzungar boundaries are moderately attested through Qing military campaign records and Russian embassy accounts; the western and southern extents toward the Kazakh steppe are conjectural, while core Ili Valley control is well-documented in Qing Veritable Records.
